lessons.title: Pre-Flight Checklist and Procedures
lessons.body: Before every flight, run a systematic pre-flight check. In Africa, dust, heat, and uneven terrain make this critical. Start with a physical inspection: check propellers for cracks or nicks, ensure motors spin freely, and confirm landing gear is secure. Inspect the battery: look for swelling, check voltage with a multimeter (e.g., 4.2V per cell for LiPo), and ensure it's charged to at least 50% for short flights. For a DJI Phantom 4, battery should read 15.2V or higher. Next, check the controller: charge level above 50%, antennas positioned correctly, and sticks move smoothly. Calibrate the compass if you've moved more than 100 km or changed locations significantly. In dusty areas, calibrate the IMU every 10 flights. Power on the drone and controller in the correct order: controller first, then drone. Wait for GPS lock: at least 10 satellites for stable hover. Check home point is set. Use a pre-flight checklist app like 'Drone Deploy' or a printed list. In rural areas, ensure no power lines or tall trees within 30 meters. Check weather: wind below 15 km/h, no rain, visibility above 5 km. For night flights, attach strobe lights. Finally, announce 'Takeoff' and clear the area. This 5-minute routine prevents 90% of crashes.

lessons.title: Basic Maneuvers: Hovering, Takeoff, Landing
lessons.body: Master these three skills before anything else. Takeoff: Stand 3-5 meters away, face the drone. Push both sticks down and inward (or use auto-takeoff). For manual takeoff, throttle up slowly until the drone lifts 1 meter, then hold. In windy conditions, take off into the wind. Hovering: The goal is to keep the drone in one spot. Use small, gentle stick movements. If the drone drifts left, tap right stick slightly right. Practice in an open field with no obstacles. In Africa, watch for sudden gustsâcompensate by lowering altitude to 2 meters where wind is weaker. Use 'Atti' mode (attitude) to learn manual control; GPS mode is easier but builds bad habits. Landing: For a safe landing, bring the drone down slowly. Reduce throttle to descend at 1 m/s. At 0.5 meters, reduce further. When it touches down, hold throttle down for 3 seconds to stop motors. In dusty areas, land on a mat or tarmac to avoid debris. Practice landing on a 1x1 meter square. Do 20 takeoffs and landings daily. For a Mavic Air 2, battery lasts about 20 minutesâso you can do many cycles. Always land with 20% battery remaining. If you can't land, hover and wait for a safe spot. In emergencies, use auto-land. These basics build muscle memory.

lessons.title: Advanced Maneuvers: Figure Eights, Banked Turns
lessons.body: Once you can hover confidently, learn figure eights and banked turns. Figure eight: Imagine two circles side by side. Start at the center, fly forward and right, then curve left to complete a circle, then cross the center and curve right to complete the other circle. Use coordinated turns: add a bit of rudder (left stick) with aileron (right stick). Keep altitude constant at 5 meters. In Africa, practice in a large open field like a soccer pitch. Banked turns: Instead of flat turns, tilt the drone into the turn. For a right bank, push right stick right and slightly down, and add left rudder. This makes turns smoother and faster. Practice at 30-degree bank angle. For a DJI Mavic 2, switch to 'Sport' mode for sharper turns, but be carefulâit's faster. Do 10 figure eights and 10 banked turns per session. Use cones or trees as markers. In windy conditions, bank into the wind to maintain course. These maneuvers are used in mapping, search and rescue, and cinematography. In African agriculture, drones use banked turns to cover fields efficiently. Always keep line of sight. If you lose orientation, switch to GPS mode and hover. Practice until you can do figure eights without thinking. This takes about 10 hours of flight time.

lessons.title: Flying in Different Weather Conditions
lessons.body: Africa's weather varies from dusty harmattan to coastal humidity. Learn to fly safely. Wind: Most consumer drones handle up to 30 km/h, but for beginners, stay below 15 km/h. Check wind with a handheld anemometer or weather app. In strong wind, fly into the wind on the way out and with it on return to save battery. Dust: In Sahel regions, dust reduces visibility and can clog motors. Use propeller guards and avoid flying in dust storms. After flight, clean with compressed air. Rain: Never fly in rainâmost drones are not waterproof. If caught, land immediately and dry with silica gel. Heat: In 40Â°C heat, batteries overheat. Fly in early morning or late afternoon. Keep batteries shaded. Cold: In highlands like Ethiopia, cold reduces battery life. Warm batteries to 20Â°C before flight. Humidity: Coastal areas cause condensation. Let drone acclimate before flying. Thunderstorms: Never flyâlightning can strike. Use a weather app like 'UAV Forecast' to check conditions. In all cases, maintain visual line of sight. If you can't see the drone, use the map. For night flying, attach strobes. In harmattan, use a filter to protect the lens. Always have a landing plan. If conditions worsen, land immediately. Practice in different conditions gradually. Start in calm mornings, then move to windy afternoons.

lessons.title: Emergency Procedures and Failsafes
lessons.body: Emergencies happen. Know how to react. First, set failsafes: In your drone app, set 'Return to Home' (RTH) altitude to 30 meters above the tallest obstacle. Set battery failsafe to trigger RTH at 20% and land at 10%. For a DJI drone, go to 'Main Controller Settings' > 'Failsafe'. Loss of signal: The drone will hover, then RTH if signal not regained. Do not panicâwait. If it doesn't return, use the map to locate it. Fly-away: If the drone drifts away, switch to 'Sport' mode and try to bring it back manually. If that fails, use 'Find My Drone' in the app. Motor failure: If a motor stops, the drone will spin. Cut throttle and let it dropâit's better than a fly-away. In Africa, emergency landing spots are often bushes. Practice emergency landings by simulating motor failure at 10 meters. Battery fire: If a battery swells or catches fire, move away and use a fire extinguisher (Class D) or sand. Never use water. Lost link: If controller dies, the drone will RTH. Always carry spare batteries for controller. Crash: If you crash, power off, check for damage. Do not fly again until repaired. Use a checklist for emergencies. In remote areas, carry a first aid kit and satellite phone. Practice these procedures monthly. For a Mavic 2, RTH can be triggered by pressing the RTH button. Know your drone's behavior. In high wind, RTH may not workâland manually. Always fly with a spotter.

lessons.title: First-Person View (FPV) Flying
lessons.body: FPV flying gives you a drone's-eye view. You'll need goggles, a drone with FPV camera, and a controller. In Africa, FPV is used for racing, inspection, and wildlife monitoring. Start with a simulator like 'VelociDrone' or 'Liftoff' on a computer. Practice 10 hours before real flight. For real FPV, use a drone like the DJI FPV or a custom build. Put on goggles, ensure antenna is connected. Take off in 'Normal' mode, then switch to 'Sport' or 'Manual'. In manual mode, the drone does not self-levelâyou must control everything. Start in an open field. Fly forward slowly, use small stick movements. To turn, bank and yaw simultaneously. In Africa, watch for birds and power lines. FPV range is limitedâstay within 500 meters. Use a spotter to watch the drone. For racing, use a 5.8GHz video transmitter. In dusty areas, protect goggles from dust. Practice figure eights in FPV. If you feel dizzy, land immediately. FPV flying is immersive but disorienting. Always have a failsafe: if signal lost, drone will cut motors (for racing) or RTH (for camera drones). In African wildlife, FPV can stress animalsâkeep distance. For inspection, use a gimbal for stable video. After flight, remove goggles and check drone. Clean lenses. FPV is not for beginnersâfirst master line-of-sight flying. Then transition. Always follow local regulations. In many African countries, FPV requires a spotter. Never fly over people. Practice in a designated area.

quiz.q: What is the recommended minimum battery voltage per cell for a LiPo battery before flight?
quiz.explanation: A fully charged LiPo cell is 4.2V; lower voltage indicates partial charge.

quiz.q: How many GPS satellites are needed for a stable hover?
quiz.explanation: At least 10 satellites ensure a stable GPS lock for hovering.

quiz.q: In dusty areas, how often should you calibrate the IMU?
quiz.explanation: Dust affects sensors, so calibrate IMU every 10 flights.

quiz.q: What is the correct order to power on a drone and controller?
quiz.explanation: Powering controller first prevents accidental drone startup.

quiz.q: What is the maximum wind speed for beginner drone pilots?
quiz.explanation: Beginners should avoid winds above 15 km/h for safety.

quiz.q: When taking off manually, how high should you lift the drone before holding?
quiz.explanation: Lift to 1 meter to clear ground effect and establish control.

quiz.q: What is the recommended descent rate for landing?
quiz.explanation: A descent rate of 1 m/s is smooth and safe for landing.

quiz.q: How long should you hold throttle down after landing to stop motors?
quiz.explanation: Hold throttle down for 3 seconds to ensure motors stop.

quiz.q: What is the recommended battery percentage to land at?
quiz.explanation: Landing at 20% battery prevents over-discharge and crash.

quiz.q: In figure eight maneuvers, what controls are coordinated?
quiz.explanation: Coordinated turns use rudder and aileron together.

quiz.q: What bank angle is recommended for practicing banked turns?
quiz.explanation: A 30-degree bank is a good starting point for smooth turns.

quiz.q: Which flight mode gives sharper turns for advanced maneuvers?
quiz.explanation: Sport mode increases responsiveness for sharper turns.

quiz.q: How many hours of practice are typically needed to master figure eights?
quiz.explanation: About 10 hours of flight time builds muscle memory for figure eights.

quiz.q: What should you do if you lose orientation during a maneuver?
options: A) Switch to GPS mode and hover
quiz.explanation: Switching to GPS mode stabilizes the drone so you can regain orientation.

quiz.q: What is the maximum wind speed most consumer drones can handle?
quiz.explanation: Most consumer drones can handle up to 30 km/h wind, but not recommended for beginners.

quiz.q: In dusty conditions, what should you use to protect the drone?
quiz.explanation: Propeller guards help keep dust out of motors and protect props.

quiz.q: What should you do if caught in rain while flying?
quiz.explanation: Most drones are not waterproof, so land immediately to avoid damage.

quiz.q: In high heat, when is the best time to fly?
options: B) Early morning or late afternoon
quiz.explanation: Flying in cooler parts of the day prevents battery overheating.

quiz.q: What should you do to batteries in cold weather before flying?
quiz.explanation: Warming batteries to 20Â°C improves performance in cold conditions.

quiz.q: Which app can help check weather conditions for drone flight?
quiz.explanation: UAV Forecast provides wind, rain, and other flight-specific weather data.

quiz.q: What is the recommended RTH altitude to clear obstacles?
quiz.explanation: Set RTH altitude to 30 meters above the tallest obstacle in your area.

quiz.q: At what battery percentage should failsafe trigger RTH?
quiz.explanation: Set battery failsafe to trigger RTH at 20% to ensure safe return.

quiz.q: What should you do if the drone has a motor failure?
options: B) Cut throttle and let it drop
quiz.explanation: Cutting throttle prevents a fly-away and reduces damage.

quiz.q: What type of fire extinguisher is safe for a LiPo battery fire?
quiz.explanation: Class D extinguishers are for metal fires, including lithium batteries.

quiz.q: What should you carry in remote areas for emergencies?
options: B) First aid kit and satellite phone
quiz.explanation: A first aid kit and satellite phone are essential for remote emergency response.

quiz.q: How many hours of simulator practice are recommended before FPV flying?
quiz.explanation: 10 hours of simulator practice builds basic FPV skills safely.

quiz.q: In FPV manual mode, what does the drone do?
quiz.explanation: Manual mode requires constant pilot input; the drone does not self-level.

quiz.q: What is the recommended maximum FPV range for beginners?
quiz.explanation: Stay within 500 meters to maintain video signal and control.

quiz.q: Why should you use a spotter when flying FPV?
options: B) To watch for obstacles and other aircraft
quiz.explanation: A spotter maintains visual line of sight and warns of hazards.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel dizzy during FPV flight?
quiz.explanation: Dizziness can lead to loss of control; land immediately for safety.
